_comment: GENERATED by src/scripts/build_catalog.sh — do not edit by hand. 'database' is what the installer's compose actually wires up; it is fixed by the installer, so `zeltro create` never asks the user to choose one for an app. Empty means the app manages its own storage internally.

apps.note: Community edition. Piece metadata is fetched from Activepieces Cloud on first boot, so the flow builder needs internet access.
Set an optional server password on first visit to restrict access.
A one-shot migration container runs before the server; the first boot takes about a minute.
nginx fronts three services: / -> Nuxt frontend, /api/ -> Go backend, /alexandrie/ -> RustFS object storage.
Pick an LLM provider and embedder in the first-run wizard; the built-in LanceDB vector store needs no extra service.
Save a config under a key at http://apprise-api/, then notify with: curl -X POST -d 'body=hi' http://apprise-api/notify/<key>
Low-code internal-tool builder. First boot takes 60-90s while it initialises. Apps are built in the browser UI, not in this project directory.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create your first admin account. Background workers are not included — use for API/SDK development and testing.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to access the archiving interface. Create a superuser with: docker exec -it archivebox-app archivebox manage createsuperuser
Bundles Elasticsearch and a background worker — budget ~3 GB RAM and ~2 minutes for the first boot.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create the admin account on first launch.
The worker container is required — it applies the blueprints that create the default login flows.
Fully client-side: PDFs never leave the browser. Some tools fetch WASM modules from a CDN on first use, so they need internet access.
Java/Spring app — first boot runs Flyway migrations and can take ~60 seconds before it answers.
Upstream is alpha-quality. Data lives in SQLite under /config — no external database is used.
Internal CouchDB and Redis are bundled — no external database needed.
Self-hosted Sentry-compatible error tracker. Create a project in the UI to get a DSN pointing at http://bugsink/.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to complete the setup wizard and create your admin account.
Open-source scheduling platform. First startup takes ~60 seconds for migrations. Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create your account.
Copy an existing Calibre library (its metadata.db) into the calibre-web-books volume, then point the first-run wizard at /books.
Upstream renamed the project to Shelfmark; sources and download clients are configured inside the web UI.
The admin key IS the dashboard login; all state lives in the shared Redis under the 'cap:' prefix.
Uptime and infrastructure monitor (formerly BlueWave Uptime). Uses the shared MongoDB.
Change the admin password on first login — it is admin/admin out of the box.
Config env vars use the CLASSICPRESS_ prefix, not WORDPRESS_, and the default table prefix is cp_.
No seeded admin and no password in the logs since v4 — sign up first, that account is the admin.
VS Code in a browser. Change the default password by editing the PASSWORD environment variable.
CodiMD has no admin account or admin UI — every user self-registers.
HTTP_ALLOWED=true is required — without it login fails over plain http.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create your admin account. Requires Docker socket access to manage deployments.
Login: no login required
AI workflow builder. First startup takes ~60 seconds for DB migrations. Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to initialize.
Uses the shared zeltro-postgres and zeltro-redis; no bundled services.
A self-signed signing certificate is generated into cert.p12 — replace it before signing anything you care about.
Do not set FORCE_SSL — Zeltro serves the app over plain http.
Delete install.php from the container once setup finishes: zeltro exec dokuwiki rm /app/dokuwiki/install.php
First boot runs the auto-installer and takes ~60 seconds before the login page appears.
First visit lands on /index.php/installation — fill in the form to create the schema and admin user.
On bridge networking there is no mDNS: devices need a fixed use_address/manual_ip or they show no status.
First boot builds the database and takes ~60 seconds. The daemon sidecar runs scheduled jobs, workflows and email fetching.
Prisma migrations run at startup; if the database is unreachable the container exits instead of serving.
Outgoing mail goes to MailHog; sign-in links appear there rather than in a real inbox.
Grab the generated password from the logs, or set your own: docker exec -it <container> filebrowser users update admin --password newpass -d /database/filebrowser.db
Server-only install: put media under the fileflows-media volume. The image is ~1 GB, so the first pull is slow.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create the admin account on first launch.
No SMTP is configured, so the 6-character sign-in code is printed in the logs: 'docker logs fizzy | grep -i code'.
First startup takes a few minutes while Flarum installs. Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ once it's ready.
Storage must be set to 'local' explicitly; Flipt v2 defaults to an in-memory backend that loses every flag on restart.
LLM workflow builder. Connect AI models and build chatbots visually.
Complete the install wizard on first visit — the DB fields are pre-filled; the first registered user becomes admin.

Help desk / shared inbox. First boot takes a few minutes. FreeScout answers 403 Untrusted Host unless the browser host matches APP_URL in docker-compose.yaml: set APP_URL to the address zeltro status prints, then zeltro down + up.
Run the web installer on first visit to create your admin account.
Admin panel is at http://$PROJECT_NAME/ghost/ — create the owner account on first visit.
Register the first user through the web UI — that account becomes admin.
Dashboard layout is driven by ./glance.yml in the project directory; Glance auto-reloads it on save.
No login required. Monitors the host system and all Docker containers.
Sentry-compatible error tracking. Point your SDK DSN at http://glitchtip/<project-id>.
Headless auto-install runs on first boot; change the four default accounts (glpi, tech, normal, post-only) right away.
On the setup form leave the site domain BLANK — a bare hostname like 'goatcounter' fails GoatCounter's two-label domain validation.
Change the admin password after first login — Gotify has no forced password reset.
Link a phone by scanning the QR code at /app/login; session data lives in the gowa-storages volume.
First boot creates an empty family tree; the first account you register becomes the tree owner.
First startup takes ~90 seconds while OpenSearch and Graylog initialize. Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ after startup.
GRIST_IN_SERVICE=true skips the /boot key gate that otherwise wedges a headless install.
Register an account on first visit. Anonymous access is enabled by default.
Uploads are stored in the heyform-assets volume; outgoing mail is not configured by default.
SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY is generated at install time — losing it makes stored integration credentials unreadable.
First visit shows the onboarding wizard. Reverse-proxy headers are pre-configured.
Home inventory manager. Data lives in SQLite under /data — no external database needed.
Config YAML lives in the homepage-config volume (/app/config); defaults are generated on first boot.
Edit ~/zeltro-projects/homer/assets/config.yml to customize your dashboard.
Runs in subpath mode: app at /, admin dashboard at /admin, backend at /backend.
First user to register becomes admin. Allow 30+ seconds after startup for migrations.
The container runs its database migrations on boot; the UI 502s for a few seconds until they finish.
Complete the setup wizard on first visit. Add media libraries after creating your admin account.
Change the default admin password immediately; sync clients point at http://joplin/.
Notebooks live in /home/jovyan/work (persisted). The image ships numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn.
Ships its own Meilisearch and headless Chrome sidecars; AI tagging stays off unless you set OPENAI_API_KEY.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create the admin account on first launch.
First boot runs the schema build and migrations — give it a minute before the admin console answers.
Place your music files in the koel-music volume then scan from the admin panel at http://$PROJECT_NAME/.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create your account on first launch.
First boot builds the component index and can take 1-2 minutes before the UI answers.
Heavy stack: web + worker + ClickHouse + S3 storage (Silo, a MinIO fork). First boot runs ClickHouse migrations and can take 2-3 minutes.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to complete setup wizard on first launch.
Federated link aggregator (Reddit alternative). Admin account set in lemmy.hjson setup block.
No model providers are configured — add an API key (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY) to the compose environment to get endpoints.
Results reflect the Docker bridge network, not your real WAN link.
First boot downloads language models — LT_LOAD_ONLY keeps that to a few hundred MB. Drop it to install every language.
SQLite-backed; the superuser is created from LD_SUPERUSER_* on first boot only.
The 'plus' image bundles Chromium for HTML snapshots — enable archiving per-bookmark or globally in Settings.
Register your account on first visit.
The master key is written to litellm-master-key.txt in the project directory — clients send it as the OpenAI API key.

Official laravel/livewire-starter-kit: Livewire 4 + Flux UI + Fortify auth (login, register, 2FA, passkeys), settings, and a dashboard. Add components with: zeltro artisan livewire make:livewire <Name>
Client-database edition: conversations live in your browser's IndexedDB, so clearing site data wipes them.
Local AWS emulator. Point the AWS CLI at it with: aws --endpoint-url=http://$PROJECT_NAME s3 ls. Needs the Docker socket so it can start Lambda containers.
First boot takes ~60 seconds while the Java API service starts.
Install wizard appears on first visit at /install/admin — create admin account there.
The pipeline project lives in /home/src/zeltro_project inside the container.
Save notebooks under the data/ folder — it is the only directory on a volume.
Federated social network. Runs migrations on first startup (~60s). Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create your account.
First visit shows the installation wizard. Complete it to set your admin account.
Create the System Admin account on first visit.
First visit shows the install wizard. Mautic requires a dedicated database user.
Rails app — the first boot runs migrations and asset setup, which takes a couple of minutes.
The setup wizard is run for you by a one-shot installer service; LocalSettings.php lives in the mediawiki-config volume.
First user to register becomes admin.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to complete setup. First startup takes ~60 seconds for JVM initialization.
Large image (multi-GB) and a slow first boot; the SQL editor answers once the HTTP API finishes loading handlers.
S3-compatible object storage. Runs Silo, the maintained MinIO fork: same S3 API, MINIO_* settings and data format. API port 9000 is internal; the web console is at http://$PROJECT_NAME/.
Runs its queue workers and scheduler internally via supervisor — no extra worker container is needed.
Register your account on first visit — no default credentials.
First boot runs the Moodle CLI installer and can take 3-5 minutes before the site responds.
Create the owner account on first visit.
Drop music into the navidrome-music volume (/music); the scanner picks it up on the next sweep.
First startup takes ~60 seconds for database migrations. Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to access.
OpenAI-compatible relay/gateway with token quotas. The default root password is fixed by upstream.
Complete the admin account setup on first visit.
Change the default password immediately after first login.
First boot installs the plugin set and can take several minutes.
Open-source Airtable alternative. First user to register becomes admin.
First boot installs and then exits once — the restart policy brings it back up serving the forum. Give it a couple of minutes.
Publish with: curl -d 'hello' http://ntfy/mytopic
First visit shows Odoo's database manager — create a database, then log in with the admin email/password you set there.
CPU-only Ollama with no preloaded model — pull one from the WebUI Models page (or via docker exec) before chatting.
SQLite-backed: everything lives in the /rails/storage volume, no shared database is used.
Git-over-SSH (port 6611) is not published — clone over HTTP.
Create an admin with: docker exec onetimesecret-app bin/ots customers create you@example.com --role colonel
Connect an IMAP / Google Workspace / M365 mailbox under Ingestion Sources to start archiving.
Create your first admin account on first visit. Ollama integration is disabled by default.
Free self-hosted instances are limited to 2 users total. Migrations run automatically on first boot (~60 seconds).
Web installer only. When it asks for the database use host zeltro-mariadb, port 3306, database orangehrm, user orangehrm, password orangehrm.
Outline requires an auth provider. Configure OIDC or email auth via env vars before first use.
First boot runs occ maintenance:install — allow a minute or two before the login page appears.
No admin account is created automatically — run the artisan command above, then log in at /admin.
Open-source design tool. Register at http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create your account. Email verification is disabled.
Add zeltro-postgres as a backup source with: postgresql://root:password@zeltro-postgres:5432/<db>?sslmode=disable
Place photos in ~/zeltro-projects/photoprism/originals/ then run 'zeltro exec photoprism-app photoprism index' to index them.
Login: register on first visit — the first account becomes admin
Federated image-sharing platform. First boot runs migrations and can take ~2 minutes. Email is wired to MailHog, so activation links land at http://zeltro-mailhog:8025/.
Open-source project management (Jira alternative). First startup takes ~60 seconds for migrations.
Privacy-first web analytics. First startup takes ~30 seconds for migrations. Create your account on first visit.
No official image exists; this uses the de-facto community build. / redirects to the admin UI because no pb_public is bundled.
Create your admin account on first visit — the setup wizard locks after 5 minutes.
Panel only — game servers additionally need a Wings daemon, which requires host Docker access and is not part of this install.
Heavy first boot — Cells runs its headless installer from install.yml, which can take a minute or two.
Sign-in sends a 6-digit code by email — read it in MailHog or with 'docker logs rallly-app'.
No SMTP is configured, so email verification / password-reset links are printed to the container log.
Keep the readeck-data volume — the auto-generated secret key lives in it, and losing it invalidates every session and token.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create the admin account on first launch. First startup runs DB migrations — allow ~30 seconds.
Roundcube is a webmail client. It requires an IMAP server to log in. In dev, MailHog is pre-configured as the outbound SMTP server.
Roll Your Own Tracker — media, fitness and reading tracker. Metadata providers (TMDB, IGDB, etc.) need internet access.
No login required — it's a public metasearch engine.
Shlink is a URL shortener API. Access the REST API at http://$PROJECT_NAME/rest/v3/. The API key is printed below. Use Shlink Web Client or the shlink CLI to manage links.
SiYuan has no user accounts. To lock it, drop SIYUAN_ACCESS_AUTH_CODE_BYPASS and add --accessAuthCode=<code> to the command.
Bookmark and link-shortener platform. Data lives in SQLite inside the slash-data volume.
Admin panel at http://$PROJECT_NAME/?admin — set the admin password on first visit. Configure IMAP/SMTP servers in the admin panel.
Setup wizard appears on first visit — create admin account there.
The backend bootstraps its own schema and a limited app DB role on first boot; give it a minute before the UI works.
Self-hosted encrypted notes server. Connect with the Standard Notes app at http://$PROJECT_NAME/. Use the Standard Notes desktop/mobile app to register and sync.
Upstream has not shipped a release since v0.3.0 (2024) and publishes no version tags, so the image is pinned by digest.
First startup takes ~2 minutes while Superset runs migrations and builds the UI. Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ when ready.
This is the SuperTokens core only. There is no web UI: point your app's SuperTokens backend SDK at http://supertokens as the connectionURI.
First boot runs Rails db:prepare against zeltro-postgres — allow ~60 seconds.
Ships a ClickHouse sidecar for event storage; first startup takes ~60 seconds. Only the first registration is allowed.
Open-source project management. Register at http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create your account. First startup takes ~60 seconds.
Create the admin user via: zeltro exec python3 manage.py createsuperuser
Tolgee's embedded Postgres is disabled — it uses the shared zeltro-postgres instead.
Low-code app builder. First startup takes ~60 seconds for migrations. Create your admin account on first visit.
Web UI only — the GPS device protocol ports (5000-5150) are not published, so real trackers cannot report in.
TrailBase normally prints a random admin password to the log; the entrypoint here resets it to a known one instead.
The maintained successor to zadam/trilium; data lives in the triliumnext-data volume.
First boot runs database migrations and can take 2-3 minutes before the UI answers.
Conversational form builder. Log in with admin@typebot.local. Viewer is at http://$PROJECT_NAME/viewer/.
Change the default admin password after the first login.
Create your admin account on first visit.
Create an account on first visit. Enable admin panel by adding ADMIN_TOKEN env var.
Image, audio and document conversion run in the browser and work fine; video conversion needs a separate vertd daemon and is not wired up.
First user to register becomes admin.
Stateless OSINT scanner. Needs outbound internet to inspect target sites; some checks stay disabled until you add third-party API keys.
First boot runs a long migration — give it a few minutes before the page answers.
Startup takes up to 5 minutes — the health check waits for Django to be ready.
Complete the setup wizard on first visit to create the admin account.
Add a TMDB API key under Settings to enable movie/TV metadata lookups.
Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/admin/ to manage your short links.
Enterprise monitoring platform. First startup takes ~60 seconds for database initialization.
Change the administrator password immediately after the first login.
Open-source team chat. First startup takes ~3 minutes for initialization. Visit http://$PROJECT_NAME/ to create your organization.
